Affiliation:: Department of Pediatrics, Health Sciences Center, University of Oklahoma
Techniques Used: Full information maximum likelihood (FIML) for missing data
Temporal Order Selection (Highest Order vs. Lowest Order)
Data & Platforms: National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health (Add Health)
CDC Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP)

Application Areas: HPV Vaccination Uptake and Stigma Reduction
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Cultural Stigma Mediation: Investigating how internalized cultural norms (e.g., feminine honor) drive health behaviors through psychological mediators like shame and purity stigma, specifically applied to HPV vaccination intentions among college women.

Advanced Longitudinal Clustering: Utilizing Vector Autoregressive (VAR) models with Lowest Order selection and Gaussian Mixture Models to identify distinct temporal trajectories and dynamic clusters in intensive longitudinal data, outperforming traditional Highest Order approaches.

High-Dimensional Variable Selection: Developing and applying Random Regularized Penalized Quasi-Likelihood (random rPQL) algorithms to perform joint variable selection in Generalized Linear Mixed Models (GLMMs), ensuring robustness in high-dimensional settings with multicollinearity.

Cross-Cultural Psychometric Invariance: Employing Confirmatory Factor Analysis and Factorial Invariance Testing to validate scales like the Honor Ideology for Manhood (HIM-R) and Womanhood (HIW) across diverse gender and ethnic groups, challenging universal conceptualizations of honor.
Summary Description: Hairong Song specializes in health psychology and epidemiology, focusing on the intersection of cultural norms, stigma, and preventive health behaviors. Her research critically examines barriers to HPV vaccination and tobacco use, particularly among young adults, by quantifying the mediating roles of honor ideologies and shame. Methodologically, she is an expert in advanced statistical modeling, including longitudinal cohort analysis, Vector Autoregressive clustering, and high-dimensional variable selection via regularized penalized quasi-likelihood. She also leads efforts in psychometric validation, ensuring measurement invariance for cultural constructs across diverse populations. Her work bridges public health interventions with rigorous statistical innovation, addressing gender-based health disparities and improving the accuracy of behavioral dynamics modeling.
